title: an undated fact on a person with two events of its type is a conflict, never a silent drop
line: assert_facts leaves an undated burial fact unasserted when the person carries two burial events, exactly as it already did for two births; the checklist raises the multi-event conflict for every type, in its own words, and a second conflict of its own naming the record whose fact fits none of them, so nothing is dropped without a word; tools/conclude.py place gives the owner a way to name which event the record's undated fact belongs to. A fact already placed can be moved to another of the person's events of its type; an event left with no statement but rejected ones leaves the person's events.

steps.say: Raymond Earl Davidson carries one Burial event already, the file's own claim, with no date
a second Burial event planted on him: the harness's own stand-in for a real second dated record, since the harness holds no such pair for him
the gravesite locator's page for his name and death year, whose row for him gives the cemetery and no date of burial

expect.why: one card, his, among the namesakes

steps.say: the owner accepts him on it: the record's undated burial fits neither of his two events, and nothing is guessed

expect.why: no third event guessed at: the record's own undated Burial asserts nothing
the checklist raises the multi-event conflict for a burial, not only a birth

question.detail_has: fits none of your 2 burial events

expect.why: and a second conflict of its own, naming the record whose undated fact fits none of them

steps.say: placing the record's Burial fact on his Birth event is refused: another type
placing it on John Y Davidson's own Burial event is refused: another person's
the owner places the record's Burial fact on the planted (second) event: the one it means
placing the same fact on the same event again is refused: its statement is already there
the plan reflects the placement: the unplaced conflict is gone, the multi-event conflict remains

question.detail_has: fits none of your 2 burial events

expect.why: the record's undated Burial fact now sits on the planted event: assert_facts's own gap is filled
two Burial events still stand on him: the multi-event conflict is not what the placement answers

steps.say: the owner moves the record's Burial statement to his first Burial event, the file's own: the planted event, left with no statement, leaves his events

expect.why: the statement moves with its status; the event it leaves has nothing left to support it
the plan, regenerated by the move, closes the multi-event conflict
